questions.question: Your team stacks many identical neural blocks that each mix information across positions and then process each position separately. Training gets shaky as you add layers. Which stabilizing idea from earlier network lessons helps most?
options: Remove all normalization and all shortcuts so the network is simpler.
Steady each block input before the heavy steps and add the original input back afterward so early signals survive.
Make the first block very deep and leave the remaining blocks empty.
Shuffle the order of the blocks randomly at every step.
questions.explanation: Remembering how steadying inputs and keeping shortcut paths stabilizes deep stacks prepares you for this lesson, which assembles those blocks into a full image encoder with a summary token.

questions.question: At hidden=768 with heads=12, what is the per-head dimension and why does it matter?
options: 12, so each head can run on a small GPU
768, because all heads share the projection
96, set by ResNet-50
64 features per Q/K/V head; twelve heads use separate 64-D subspaces, and scaled attention divides by sqrt(64)
questions.explanation: head_dim = hidden / heads = 64. Each head has a separate 64-D Q/K/V subspace; the attention matrix itself is T×T, and scaled dot-product attention divides its logits by sqrt(64).

questions.question: Does the ViT encoder need a causal attention mask?
options: No: the encoder is bidirectional, every token may attend to every other token in the same sequence
Yes, like a GPT decoder
Only for the CLS row
Only during training
questions.explanation: Vision encoders are bidirectional. Causal masking appears later when a text decoder consumes the cross-attention output.

questions.question: What does the CLS token's final hidden state represent after all 12 blocks?
options: A copy of the input embedding
A learned vector summary of the entire image that downstream heads project into class logits or contrastive embeddings
Random noise
The last patch only
questions.explanation: The CLS token starts empty and accumulates information from every patch through self-attention across all 12 blocks.

questions.question: With hidden=768 and mlp_ratio=4.0, what does FeedForward construct?
options: Linear(768, 768) followed by GELU and Linear(768, 768)
A 12-head attention layer with 64-dimensional values
Linear(768, 3072) followed by GELU and Linear(3072, 768)
Linear(3072, 768) followed by GELU and Linear(768, 3072)
questions.explanation: FeedForward computes inner=int(768*4.0)=3072, then applies fc1, GELU, and fc2 to return to the hidden width of 768.

questions.question: What changes if a register token is prepended to this encoder sequence?
options: The model becomes a causal decoder and masks image tokens
Every patch is removed so the sequence length stays fixed
The token embedding dimension changes from 768 to 64
The sequence gains a learned token; the attention and FFN dimensions stay the same
questions.explanation: A register is an additional learned sequence element. Existing block projections still use the same hidden width; only the token count and the corresponding attention matrices grow.
